newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two bids for Svyazinvest, minister says.
newsitem.headline: Two bids for Svyazinvest, minister says.

text.p: The Russian government has received two bids for the stake of 25 percent plus one share it is auctioning in telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Bulgak said on Friday.

He told Ekho Moskvy radio that the bids had been received from Russian consortia, both of which have the participation of foreign investors. Results of the auction are due to be announced after 5 p.m. (1300 GMT).

"As far as I know, two bids have been received in which some Russian banks took part with the participation of foreign capital," said Bulgak, who is responsible for science policy and was previously Telecommunications Minister, a post which no longer exists.

A group around Russia's Uneximbank and Bank MFK (ICFC) is bidding, officials from the group have said, and industry sources say Russia's Alfa-Bank and Most-Bank are also likely to bid. Spain's Telefonica has said it was taking part in a Russian-international consortium bidding for the stake, for which the starting price is $1.18 billion.
Bulgak said France Telecom, Germany's Deutsche Telekom and U.S. group Sprint had been considering a bid but had decided not to.

Svyazinvest owns controlling stakes in 88 regional and other telcoms companies, including long-distance operators Rostelekom. The government intends to sell a further 24 percent stake to Russian investors later this year or next, reducing its stake to 51 percent.
